# The RT64 shaders the web page builds: one shader description a line, other mode L and H, color combiner L and H,
# flags, in hex. RT64 specializes each one's WGSL when the page is built and builds them with the game waiting: those
# above the first "section" line before the game starts, and a section when a frame first wants 4 of its shaders, so
# that nothing draws with the ubershader, which integrated graphics can't afford (N64Recomp-browser's README, "Give
# RT64 a list of the game's shaders").
#
# Recorded by playing, a page load a section: N64Recomp-browser's tools/record_shaders.mjs with
# tools/shader_plan.json, which drives the menus with the default keys (A on X, the stick on the arrow keys) and knows
# where the game is by gGameSettings (tools/game_state.js). Section 0 is the launcher, the Controller Pak screen, the
# logos, the intro, the title and the menus to a Single Race: One Player, Race Type, Opponents, Difficulty, Track
# Select, Car Select, Transmission, the Rumble Pak screen and the loading card. Then a Single Race on each of the two
# tracks Track Select offers a new save, driven as tools/play_plan.json drives (backing out of what the car is stuck
# against on Coventry Cove only), 70 s of the race's clock from its load (its flyover and countdown included):
# Coventry Cove, and Mount Mayhem (one Right at Track Select) twice, the second time in the yellow car (a second
# Right, which Car Select takes). Not recorded: the tracks a save opens later, Championship's screens between races,
# Time Attack, Two Player's split screen, Beetle Battle and a race's end. Flags follow settings (filtering, HDR,
# upscaling), so a change to one of those defaults means recording again. The shaders tools/play_plan.json's plays
# missed, where its car went other ways, were added by hand: 4 in section 0 and 17 in Coventry Cove's.
